analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and אֶל־הָאָדָם identifies the man as the one addressed. The following question אַיֶּכָּה (“Where are you?”) gives the words spoken to him.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים אֶל הָאָדָם, יַהְוֶה names the God who calls to the man. The following אֱלֹהִים is in apposition to the name.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. The singular verbs וַיִּקְרָא (“he called”) and וַיֹּאמֶר (“he said”) identify one speaker addressing the man.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים אֶל הָאָדָם, אֶל marks the man as the person God calls to. The following וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ, “and he said to him,” confirms the addressee.
God calls אֶל הָאָדָם, “to the man.” The singular לוֹ, “to him,” and אַיֶּכָּה, “where are you?” identify the man as the individual being addressed.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun with prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the speaker. לוֹ identifies the man as the addressee, and אַיֶּכָּה (“Where are you?”) gives the words spoken.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add the locative interrogative אַי under אי, including its use with a personal suffix.
draft.definition: Ask where a person or thing is. A pronominal suffix can identify the person whose location is asked about.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:9 the suffix identifies the addressee. In Genesis 4:9 the question אֵי הֶבֶל אָחִיךָ names Abel as the person being sought.

analysis.evidence: Yahweh God calls אֶל הָאָדָם, “to the man,” and וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ, “he said to him,” introduces the question. The suffix on אַיֶּכָּה addresses that man directly and אַי asks his location.
analysis.morphology: Interrogative adverb with the second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ־כָּה.
